e-211.knowledge_point: Calculating the Velocity of a Particle
e-211.problem: The position $x$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by $x(t) = 3t^2 +3t +1.$ Calculate the velocity at time $t.$
e-211.worked_solution:
The velocity is the derivative of the position function $x(t)$ with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}+3t+1) \\  & =6t+3\end{aligned}
$$

e-212.knowledge_point: Calculating the Velocity of a Particle at a Particular Moment
e-212.problem: The position $x,$ measured in meters, of a particle at time $t$ is given by $x(t) = 6t^4 -3t^2 +t,$ where $t$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the velocity at time $t=1$.
e-212.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{4}-3{t}^{2}+t) \\  & =24{t}^{3}-6t+1\end{aligned}
$$

 
To calculate the velocity at $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the velocity function above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =24(1)^{3}-6(1)+1 \\  & =24-6+1 \\  & =19\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity of the particle is $19\,\textrm{m/s}.$

e-214.knowledge_point: Calculating the Speed of a Particle at a Particular Moment
e-214.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle (in meters) at time $t$ seconds is given by 

$$
s(t) = t^2 - 36t,\quad t\geq 0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle when $t=1\,\textrm{s}$.
e-214.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-36t) \\  & =2t-36\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=1,$ the velocity is

$$
v(1) = 2(1) - 36 = -34.
$$

Therefore, the speed is $|{-34}| = 34\, \textrm{m/s}.$

Question 5
?

The position x of a particle at time t is given by x(t)=2t3+e2t. Calculate the velocity at time t.

a
v(t)=3t3+2et
b
v(t)=6t2+2e2t
c
v(t)=6t3+2et
d
v(t)=2t2+2e2t
e
v(t)=3t2+e2t
Submit

decision.explanation: Velocity is the derivative of position. The power rule gives d(2t³)/dt=6t², and the chain rule gives d(e^(2t))/dt=2e^(2t). Thus option b is correct.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: The position $x$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by $x(t)=2{t}^{3}+{e}^{2t}.$ Calculate the velocity at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
The velocity is the derivative of the position function $x(t)$ with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}+{e}^{2t}) \\  & =6{t}^{2}+2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}
$$

The displacement s (in meters) relative to a fixed origin O of a particle moving in a straight line along the x-axis is given by the equation s(t)=(2t+1)3, where t is the time, measured in seconds. Find the position and velocity of the particle at the initial moment of time t=0s.

a

b
s0=4.5m,v0=2.5m/s
c
s0=4.5m,v0=2m/s
d
s0=3m,v0=6m/s
e
s0=1m,v0=2.5m/s

decision.explanation: At t=0, s(0)=(2·0+1)^3=1 m. By the chain rule, v(t)=s'(t)=6(2t+1)^2, so v(0)=6 m/s. Thus option a is correct.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: The displacement $s$ (in meters) relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by the equation $s(t)=(2t+1)^{3}$, where $t$ is the time, measured in seconds. Find the position and velocity of the particle at the initial moment of time $t=0\,\text{s}.$
after.worked_solution:
To calculate the initial position, we substitute $t=0$ it into the equation $s(t)=(2t+1)^{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{0} & =s(0) \\  & =(2\cdot 0+1)^{3} \\  & ={1}^{3} \\  & =1\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((2t+1)^{3}) \\  & =6(2t+1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the velocity at $t=0\,\text{s},$ we substitute $t=0$ into the velocity function above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{0} & =v(0) \\  & =6(2\cdot 0+1)^{2} \\  & =6(1)^{2} \\  & =6\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$
